name: shinny

attributes.attribute: ball game played at the winter solstice

sources: Monaghan, Patricia. The Encyclopedia of Celtic Mythology and Folklore. Checkmark Books, 2008.
text: Shinny is a Scottish ritual. It is a ball game played at the winter solstice. The game is a little like hurling. Teams drive a stick or club across open ground. The winter solstice is the shortest day of the year. People marked that turning point to play. The game gave the dark season a burst of motion. Few details of the rules survive. The name shinny still names a rough field game in Scotland. It ties a sport to the swing of the sun.
